match.reason: The closest bank point, Liveability for everyone, covers different needs by age and ability with a focus on accessibility, but it does not teach that people are drawn to places they see as liveable or that income and culture also change what counts as liveable.

draft.title: Liveability and where people live
card: People tend to move to, and stay in, places they see as liveable. A place that seems to offer a good quality of life draws people in.
Liveability is seen through a person's own needs. Two people can look at the same place and judge it differently.
What counts as liveable can differ with age, income, culture and needs. A family with young children may want good schools and parks. A retiree may want quiet streets and nearby health care.
A person on a low income may put housing costs first. Someone whose culture is linked to a community may want to live close to that community.
draft.remember: People are drawn to places they see as liveable, and what they see as liveable depends on who they are and what they need.

a.q: Why might a place be a good choice for one household but a poor choice for another?
opts: Households judge it by their own needs and circumstances
Liveability is a fixed score that people can only accept
Only the household with more income can judge it fairly
The place changes its services for each new household
a.why: Liveability depends on what a person needs, such as their age, income or culture, so households can judge the same place differently. It is not a fixed score that everyone must accept in the same way.
a.clue: Think about who is judging the place.

b.q: Sam is a retiree who is choosing a town to live in. Which feature is she most likely to see as making a town liveable?
opts: Quiet streets and health care close by
A large number of schools for young children
Low-cost housing near a big student campus
Many playgrounds and sports fields for teenagers
b.why: A retiree is likely to value quiet and easy access to health care. Schools and playgrounds matter most to families with children, so they are less likely to be her first choice.
b.clue: Think about what suits someone's age and needs.

a.best: Households judge it by their own needs and circumstances

b.best: Quiet streets and health care close by
